items.text: Two men or two women should be able to marry each other, just as a man and a woman can.
items.rationale: Same-sex marriage recognition; review rewrite of draft 01 (drops 'any two adults' kinship reading). Law varies by country, so good frame contrast.

items.text: An adult's sex as recorded on official documents should be whatever they declare, without needing medical diagnosis or treatment.
items.note: Official documents: records such as ID cards, passports and birth certificates.
items.rationale: Strong self-ID stance; review rewrite of draft 03 (adults only, neutral 'sex as recorded'). A progressive item many moderates reject.

items.text: If one spouse wants to end the marriage, that spouse should be able to divorce without proving the other did wrong.
items.rationale: No-fault divorce; condition (one spouse wants out) favours Progressive. Draft 02 with review's 'that spouse' fix; not a logical mirror of pro-07.

items.text: If a woman in early pregnancy decides against having a child, she should be allowed to end the pregnancy.
items.note: About what is permitted, not about penalties. Abortion law partly overlaps the Liberty vs security axis; disclosed.
items.rationale: Abortion on request in early pregnancy; condition (her own decision) favours Progressive. Rewrite of draft 04 ('available' was ambiguous).

items.text: Boys and girls should be raised the same way, with the same toys, clothes and chores.
items.rationale: Strong egalitarian stance on gendered custom; replaces drafts 06/07 (process-only and cross-loading on Newcomers) per review.

items.text: Abortion should be allowed only in rare cases, such as rape or a threat to the woman's life.
items.note: About what is permitted, not about penalties. Abortion law partly overlaps the Liberty vs security axis; disclosed.
items.rationale: Mainstream pro-life-with-exceptions view, not a total ban; draft 12 with review wording fixes. A traditional item many moderates endorse.

items.text: In a marriage, the husband should have the final say on major family decisions.
items.rationale: Complementarian household headship, a strong traditional view adherents recognise; replaces content-free drafts 13/14 (blind audit: unclear).

items.text: If a couple has young children and there is no abuse, they should stay married even when the marriage is unhappy.
items.rationale: Marriage as a lasting duty to children; condition (young children, no abuse) favours Traditional. Draft 09 kept per review.

items.text: If a child needs adoptive parents, a mother and a father should be preferred over two mothers or two fathers.
items.rationale: Preference for mother-father homes; review rewrite of draft 08 (removed double-barrelled 'married'). Condition (a child needing a home) favours Traditional.

items.text: Sex should be kept for marriage.
items.rationale: Strong traditional sexual norm, discriminates well across cultures; added per review to cover non-LGBT sexual morality.
